title: A randomized purpose intervention changed worker performance, retention, priorities, and parental-leave behavior
source_unit: 2,976 white-collar employees in a firm randomized to a worker-centered purpose intervention or comparison condition

observations.period: Two-year randomized rollout; NBER Working Paper 33843, May 2025

denominator.unit: white-collar employees enrolled in the randomized rollout

low_performer_path.value: low performers either left the firm or improved in their current jobs

meaning_pay_tradeoff.value: trade-off between meaning and pay flattened as low-meaning/high-pay workers left

parental_leave.value: uptake increased and gender gaps in preferences and behaviors narrowed

bonuses.value: higher bonuses shared returns between firm and employees

observations.method: Randomized rollout of a firm worker-centered intervention, described as enabling employees to reduce the cost of effort by discovering purpose, followed for two years with performance, retention, stated priorities, behavior, parental-leave, and compensation outcomes.
observations.uncertainty: The experiment is firm-specific and limited to white-collar employees; the public abstract does not identify the exact treatment content, implementation heterogeneity, worker household outcomes, or external validity to hourly, platform, public-sector, or nonunion workers.
observations.subgroup: Employees in the participating firm; the source highlights low performers and gender differences in preferences and behaviors.
observations.counterinterpretation: Observed performance gains may arise through selection/retention and managerial or compensation responses rather than a uniform increase in worker autonomy; leaving the firm is an outcome that can improve firm performance while shifting risk to workers.

boundary: This record adds a firm-level randomized meaning-to-work-outcome route: a purpose intervention changed performance, retention pathways, stated priorities, parental-leave behavior, and bonuses. It does not establish household welfare, durable worker control, bargaining power, broad labor-market generalization, or political action.
